jobs.title: Jobs register & change-tracking traceability
jobs.description: Add a SpecPad-owned jobs register (jobs.json) with an open/closed lifecycle, the active-job governance rule, the editor Jobs view and active-job picker, and the skill git plumbing so every spec change traces to a job. Baselined at v1.1.

jobs.title: Onboarding: specpad init
jobs.description: One-command setup that scaffolds docs/specpad/, installs the pre-push hook, wires the SpecPad working-loop directive into the project CLAUDE.md, and generates the launcher — so a new user is fully set up on install with no manual configuration. Idempotent and non-destructive.

jobs.title: Baseline generator (draft a spec from existing code)
jobs.description: An agent procedure that bootstraps a draft v1 SRS/VTP from an existing codebase — surveying modules, public behavior, and existing tests — so SpecPad can be adopted on a project that did not start with it. Output is a draft for human ratification, mapped to existing tests, governance-clean.

jobs.title: Requirement audit (reconcile spec with code)
jobs.description: An agent procedure that reconciles the existing SRS/VTP against the whole codebase, reporting drift both directions — code behavior with no requirement (missing), requirements whose behavior is gone/changed (stale), and requirements/test references with no covering test (coverage). Reports ratifiable proposals; applies nothing destructive. The commit-time audit is its staged-diff form.

jobs.title: Spec reconciliation (apply requirement-audit findings)
jobs.description: Apply the ratified findings from the first requirement audit: add the missing recent-projects requirement (EDS-12) mapped to its existing tests, correct the stale ValidationPanel test reference (TEST-22 -> StatusBar), and close two of the four not_tested coverage gaps (TEST-9 id-immutability, TEST-59 records-only) with real tests.

jobs.title: Jobs view as release notes
jobs.description: Reframe the editor Jobs tab as release notes: group jobs by major version (unversioned under Unreleased), then by type into Features and Bugfixes, with each job's description beneath its title. Clicking a job opens a separate detail view. Adds the job record type and version fields and moves Jobs to the leftmost tab.

jobs.title: Closed-job change cache, owner, derived version, in-progress vs released views
jobs.description: On close, cache a job's before/after spec snapshots (lockfile-class) so the browser editor can show its SRS/VTP changes; add an owner set from git at creation; derive a job's version from the release tag containing its commits; split the Jobs tab into In progress (open) and Released (closed) views.

jobs.title: Source-code traceability (job to commits to code)
jobs.description: Cache each closed job's commit list (commits.json, derived from the Job: trailer) so the editor shows a job's commits alongside its SRS/VTP changes, and document the skill's source-traceability export (per-job commits + code diffs from git) that feeds the eQMS evidence package.

jobs.title: Architecture spec (arc42 + C4) and Architecture view
jobs.description: Add an optional architecture spec — an arc42 software architecture document (markdown) plus a C4 model in Structurizr DSL — tracked under docs/specpad/, job/release coupled (no requirement-level trace matrix). New editor Architecture view renders the arc42 doc and presents the C4 DSL. Dogfooded with SpecPad's own SAD.

jobs.title: Architecture templates (generic + medical), init path quiz, beefed-up generic SAD
jobs.description: Ship two architecture profiles — a beefed-up generic arc42+C4 template (several diagrams, no safety classification) and a medical template (62304/FDA: per-unit classification, segregation, verification) — each with a soft authoring guide. The init quiz lets the user pick generic vs medical and scaffolds the match. Re-dogfood SpecPad's SAD with the richer generic template. Cybersecurity architecture is a noted coming-soon pillar.

jobs.title: Architecture Edit/Display view: CodeMirror editor, markdown rendering, diagram SVG
jobs.description: Give the Architecture tab Edit/Display sub-tabs: a syntax-highlighting CodeMirror editor for the arc42 markdown and C4 source, and a Display that renders the markdown as HTML (react-markdown) with inline diagram SVGs (draw.io export) and the authoring-guide panel. Diagram change tracking stays coarse (file changed: yes/no). draw.io is the pragmatic diagram source; SVG export is rendered client-side.

jobs.title: Diagram-heavy architecture: markdown-placed inline diagrams; Structurizr DSL optional
jobs.description: Let the arc42 markdown define where diagrams go via image references; the Display renders each referenced SVG inline at its place. Ship several diagrams (Context overview near the top, Building Block interfaces, Runtime process, Deployment) and demote the Structurizr/C4 DSL to an optional alternative (loader kept, editor shows it only when present, removed from default templates + SpecPad's dogfood).

jobs.title: Architecture changes in the job detail (coarse file-level + SAD line diff)
jobs.description: Snapshot the architecture files (sad.md, diagrams, guide, optional dsl) into the closed-job cache, and show an Architecture changes section in the job detail: which arch files were added/modified/removed (coarse), plus an added/removed-line diff for the SAD markdown. Completes SAD-4. Diagrams stay coarse (no in-diagram deltas).

jobs.title: Split into core specpad + optional specpad-medical add-on skill
jobs.description: Extract medical/regulatory content into a separate specpad-medical add-on skill (62304/FDA profile, medical template + guide, regulatory governance), keeping core specpad lean and general (generic profile, contract, jobs, working loop). The contract and editor stay unified (medical features light up only when a medical profile is present). Controls bloat: the regulated layer's token cost is paid only when opted in.

jobs.title: Formal Release entity: release-as-jobs view + full-doc release snapshot
jobs.description: Make a release first-class: a release is its set of jobs at a version, with a guaranteed full snapshot of all key docs and a Releases view that reads as release notes (jobs grouped per release). Core feature. Dogfooded by cutting v1.2.

jobs.title: Product requirements (PRD) register + integrations design addendum
jobs.description: Add an optional product-requirements (PRD) register as an SRS-shaped peer document, with upward SRS→PRD traceability (satisfies, by id) and opt-in governance (prd-referential-integrity, prd-coverage) that costs nothing without a PRD register. Capture the integrations design addendum (Jira/Confluence ingest add-on, import vs baseline routing, multi-repo system-level docs, PRD/validation, usability/interface-spec) as forward design. Dogfooded: SpecPad gains its own PRD register and SRS→PRD links.

jobs.title: Auditor view — live design-control evidence (coverage, trace matrix, gaps)
jobs.description: Add an Auditor view (editor tab) that renders a reviewer's-eye picture of the open project: a coverage summary (requirements verified, test results, product-requirement coverage), the PRD→SRS→VTP traceability matrix with per-requirement verification results, and a gap list derived from the shared governance check plus the proposed-PRD roadmap. Load the optional PRD register into the editor so product requirements and upward traces are available. Includes a scope disclaimer (evidence that supports design controls; not a QMS / compliance determination).

jobs.title: Editor visual system: design tokens, themes, Overview landing, tab reorder
jobs.description: Polish the editor into a cohesive, modern product. Build a CSS design-token system and ship three selectable themes (developer tool, editorial, blueprint) with a menubar switcher persisted to localStorage (applied before first paint, no flash). Add an Overview (Home) landing — an engineer's status home showing in-progress jobs, the latest release, and a coverage/health headline, with quick navigation into the authoring views — and make it the default view. Reorder the document tabs to lead with Overview then the authoring views, grouping the oversight views (Auditor, Releases, Jobs) after; this supersedes JV-4's leftmost-Jobs rule (changed under this job, not JOB-6).

jobs.title: On-demand authoring guides (requirements, tests, PRD, architecture)
jobs.description: Add per-document-type authoring guides under skill/specpad/guides/ that the skill reads just-in-time (progressive disclosure) rather than inlining into the always-on prompt. Each guide covers what to capture, how to phrase/structure, and good vs bad examples with the reason each is good or bad. SKILL.md gains a lean routing table that points to each guide at its working-loop touchpoint without duplicating the content. A parity test keeps SKILL.md and the guides in sync (no orphaned or dangling guides). Medical/regulatory authoring overlays remain a future addition in the specpad-medical add-on (opt-in).

jobs.title: Design-control map in the Auditor view; trace matrix moves to its own Traceability tab
jobs.description: Turn the Auditor view into an orientation index for a reviewer: a design-control map listing each formal element (Design Inputs, Outputs, Verification, Validation, Traceability, Design Changes, Design History File, Design Reviews, Risk Management, Configuration Management) with its standard citation (IEC 62304 / 21 CFR 820.30), a plain statement, a status derived live from the project, and a link to the section/tab holding the evidence — so an engineer can answer 'where are your design inputs?' instantly. Move the per-requirement trace matrix (and the coverage summary and gap list) to its own Traceability tab; the Auditor view links to it.

jobs.title: Show the active job's in-progress (uncommitted) changes in the Jobs view
jobs.description: Make an open job's changes visible before it is closed. Snapshot a job's before spec state into .specpad/jobs/<id>/before/ when the job is created (not only on close), pinning its starting point. The Jobs view then renders the active open job's in-progress changes by diffing that before snapshot against the live working copy (SRS/VTP) — so uncommitted and unreleased work shows up, the same diff the requirements/verification tables already display, attributed to the job.

jobs.title: Active job's in-progress architecture (SAD) changes in the Jobs view
jobs.description: Extend the in-progress change view to architecture. The before snapshot taken at job creation now captures the full key doc set (proj/srs/vtp + SAD markdown, diagrams, guide, and a per-state arch-files manifest), matching the close cache. The Jobs view then shows the active open job's architecture changes (added/modified/removed files, coarse, plus a SAD line diff) by diffing that before snapshot against the working SAD/diagrams — completing the srs/vtp/sad set for in-progress work.

jobs.title: Cut release v1.3
jobs.description: Cut release v1.3: close JOB-15..22 and set their version to v1.3, regenerate their before/after/commit caches, refresh the baseline snapshot (preserving v1.2 as an older snapshot), and add the v1.3 entry to the releases manifest. Release bookkeeping using the existing Release entity (REL-1..3) — no new product behavior.

jobs.title: Marketing site refresh — vision and feature list
jobs.description: Refresh specpad.com messaging (keeping the look & feel) to reflect v1.3: a balanced/dual hero (specs that live in your repo AND design-control evidence), and a feature list covering the full chain — product requirements (PRD), software requirements + verification, the traceability matrix and Auditor design-control map (IEC 62304 / 21 CFR 820.30), architecture, change control via jobs (in-progress + released diffs), releases as checkpoints, governance, themes, and the eQMS-export direction. Marketing copy only — non-behavioural.

jobs.title: Document-type registry — single source of truth; snapshot/diff/validation built from it
jobs.description: Introduce src/shared/docTypes.ts as the registry of content document types (srs, vtp, prd; future soup/sdd/cyber) — each with kind (id-keyed register / prose / asset), file naming, schema, baseline membership, and generator scope. Build validation and the schema reference from it. Make snapshot/diff loaders document-type-generic so a newly registered register type flows into release/baseline snapshots, per-job diffs, and the redline with no code changes. Generalize the skill's snapshot/cache prose to 'every document in the project index plus the architecture files'.

jobs.title: PRD editing tab + redline in the editor
jobs.description: Add a Product Requirements tab to the editor that edits the PRD register (text/code/status/tags, add/delete) and shows the since-baseline redline (the diff plumbing is registry-generic from JOB-25). PRD status (proposed/implemented) is editable since it drives prd-coverage and the Auditor map. Built on the document-type registry.

jobs.title: Baseline generator + adoption default to PRD and architecture
jobs.description: Make the full design-control set the default when adopting SpecPad on an existing repo: the baseline generator drafts, by default, a PRD (user needs / product intent, proposed for ratification, with SRS items linked up via satisfies) and a starter arc42 SAD (context + building-block diagram) in addition to SRS/VTP. init/import default to the full set, each proposed for ratification (a project may decline a type). Broaden the demo manifest regex so every content document type is carried, not a fixed list. Skill prose, registry-aware (drafts the project's configured document types).

jobs.title: PRD tab downward trace + design-control phase bands under the tabs
jobs.description: In the Product Requirements tab, show each item's downward trace — the software requirements that satisfy it (a Satisfied-by column), flagging an implemented PRD item with no satisfying requirement. And render a thin band below the document tabs labelling each design-control phase, spanning the tabs it covers (Design Inputs across Product Requirements + Requirements; Design Verification across Verification Tests + Results; Design Outputs = Architecture; Traceability; Design History = Releases; Design Changes = Jobs).

jobs.title: Per-job impact evaluation across every registered document type (+ bring the SAD current)
jobs.description: Generalize the working loop so a job evaluates its impact on EVERY registered document type — not just SRS/VTP. Register architecture (the SAD) as a document type so the registry is the complete list of impactable docs; the working loop (SKILL.md + CLAUDE.specpad.md) iterates the project's registered types (product requirements, requirements, verification, architecture, and any future pillar) and updates each affected one in the same job, spec-first — the same registry-generic approach used for the diffs. Apply it by bringing SpecPad's own SAD current (it had drifted since v1.2: no PRD, registry, Auditor, themes).

jobs.title: Editor authoring-view consistency (PRD/VTP parity, SRS rename, chronological tabs) + section-aware architecture diffs
jobs.description: Make the PRD and VTP tables consistent with the SRS table: PRD hides Tags/Status (assume implemented; flag proposed in red under the code + italic text), uses the row hamburger (add/move/delete/view info), and shows Satisfied-by as an expandable Tests-style toggle; VTP hides Result (this is the plan, not the results), uses the row hamburger, moves history into the info dialog, and shows Verifies as an expandable Tests-style toggle. Rename the SRS view to Software Requirements (it was just 'Requirements', confusing next to Product Requirements). Order the tabs chronologically through the design-control phases (Inputs -> Outputs -> Verification -> Controls -> Traceability -> History -> Changes). Make architecture diffs section-aware: markdown files report what changed per heading; diagrams report 'Diagram changed'.

jobs.title: Release-cut jobs auto-close as the final step before the release
jobs.description: A release is cut under a job (e.g. 'Cut release vX'). That job is the release's final act and must close itself as the last step before the tag, so no 'Cut release' job is ever left open after its release ships (its derived version is that release, because the tag contains its commit). Document the cutting-a-release procedure in the skill and retroactively close the stale JOB-23 ('Cut release v1.3').

jobs.title: Verification evidence — VTP→test→run chain (linkage + run capture + Results chain view)
jobs.description: Establish the framework-agnostic verification evidence chain: a VTP item links to its automated test(s) via a stored, id-keyed automation field ({runner,file,selector}); a normalized RunRecord captures an actual run's per-test outcomes (parsed from the runner's machine report, e.g. vitest --reporter=json) stamped with the commit/date; the editor's Results tab shows and edits the full chain (VTP→automation→run status), deriving automated results from the run instead of hand-asserting them; run records are frozen for key deliverables (release baseline + job close). Core stays test-framework agnostic (runner/selector opaque; adapters or CI emit the normalized record). Phase 1 of the verification-evidence design.

jobs.title: Verification rollups — per-job verification status in the Jobs view + an Overview headline
jobs.description: Phase 2 of verification evidence. Surface the captured run as roll-ups that complete the design-control loop: a job's detail shows the verification status of the tests it added/modified (derived from the run) with a pass/not-run/fail summary; the Overview shows an overall verification headline. Uses the latest captured run; per-release/per-job frozen runs (frozen on close/cut) light up the same panels for historical checkpoints.

jobs.title: Cut release v1.4
jobs.description: Release v1.4: closed the done-but-open jobs (JOB-24..28, JOB-33), set version v1.4 on JOB-23..34, moved the v1.3 baseline to snapshots/v1.3, regenerated the v1.4 baseline and froze the verification run into it. Per the release-cut procedure (JOB-31), this cut job closes itself as the final step before the v1.4 tag.

jobs.title: Fault-tolerant diagram loading (unresolvable ref no longer aborts project open)
jobs.description: The editor no longer fails to open a project when a diagram reference in the SAD points at a missing or invalid path — the reference degrades to a missing-diagram placeholder and the rest of the project loads normally.
jobs.technical_notes: loadProjectText rethrew any non-NotFound error, so an unresolvable diagram reference (a missing file, or a path with segments the File System Access API rejects with 'Name is not allowed') aborted the whole open with 'Failed to open project'. Fix: walk nested path segments so a subdirectory reference resolves, and catch every failure mode of the resolver — degrade to a missing diagram rather than throwing.

jobs.title: Row-actions menu z-order — render the open menu above surrounding table content
jobs.description: The per-row hamburger (⋮) menu on the requirements, verification, and PRD tables now paints above surrounding rows instead of being clipped by them.
jobs.technical_notes: Root cause: the dropdown was an absolutely-positioned element with a small z-index nested inside a table row, and each row's fade-in animation (animating transform) establishes a stacking context that traps the menu inside its row — so later rows paint over the part that overflows downward. Fix: render the open menu (and its backdrop) in a portal to document.body with fixed positioning anchored to the trigger, at a popover-level z-index, so it can never be trapped by a row/column stacking context. Close on scroll/resize so the menu stays anchored to the trigger.

jobs.title: Committed .claude/skills/specpad mirror of the distributable skill
jobs.description: Contributors working on this repo should have the specpad skill active in Claude Code with zero setup on clone. skill/specpad/ remains the canonical source of the distributable product (the folder that gets zipped as specpad-skill.zip). .claude/skills/specpad/ is added as a committed installed copy, treated as a build artifact of skill/specpad/. Drift is prevented by a pre-push hook check plus an `npm run sync-skill` command that regenerates the mirror. Cross-platform, no symlink or Developer-Mode dependency on Windows.

jobs.title: SKILL.md jobs.json shape & code-naming ambiguity
jobs.description: Ship a starter template for the jobs register and name its top-level `jobs` array in SKILL.md, plus make the JOB-<n> code convention explicit, so downstream projects can't guess the shape wrong.
jobs.technical_notes: Root cause of the crash a downstream rimsys-sync adoption hit: (a) templates/ shipped starter files for proj/srs/vtp/prd/releases but not for jobs, so the skill inferred the shape from SKILL.md prose; (b) the jobs-register section described the record shape but never named the top-level `jobs` field, so `items` (used by srs/vtp/prd) was a plausible guess and became rimsys-sync.jobs.json, which then blew up on `.find` in the editor. Fix upstream in skill/specpad/: add templates/starter.jobs.json matching JobsDoc (src/shared/schema.ts:297), and make SKILL.md name the top-level `jobs: []` field explicitly. Also prescribe `JOB-<n>` monotonic (rather than leaving it project-local and inviting thematic codes).

jobs.title: Split job description into release-note description + engineer technical_notes
jobs.description: Give the jobs register two altitudes: a short release-note-voice `description` (what a user sees in the changelog) and an optional engineer-voice `technical_notes` (root cause, mechanism, files touched). Both stay prose and validation-optional; no governance rule.
jobs.technical_notes: Add `technical_notes?: string` to `JobRecord` and `jobsSchema.properties` in src/shared/schema.ts; update the sidecars.test.ts records-only assertion to include the new key. Extend SKILL.md's cache-files bullet and Jobs-register section with an altitude rule, a before/after example, and a one-line migration note. Add an example record to templates/starter.jobs.json showing the split. Editor renders `technical_notes` only in the job detail view (as a secondary field under Description), not in the release-notes list. Do not auto-migrate existing files; opportunistically clean up SpecPad's own open jobs (JOB-35, JOB-36, JOB-38). Dogfood as JOBS-13.

jobs.title: Multi-user self-hosted server — edit the spec without source access
jobs.description: Staff without a clone of the repository — quality and product managers — can now edit requirements and verification tests in the SpecPad editor through a server their company hosts, signing in with corporate SSO and publishing their changes with an explicit Commit button. Their edits arrive in the repository as ordinary git commits authored by them.
jobs.technical_notes: See docs/design/specpad-server-design.md. Three parts: (1) a FileApi transport seam in the editor so the same UI runs against local files, the read-only demo, or a server; (2) src/shared/merge.ts — a pure item-id-keyed three-way merge, the reason concurrent editing is safe and the reason SpecPad JSON is never merged textually; (3) a server workspace in this repo owning a bare clone plus one sparse-checked-out git worktree per user, with a pluggable AuthProvider (proxy/oidc/dev) yielding a Principal. Identity is deliberately separate from the git push credential: SSO supplies the commit author, a machine credential does the push. Commit pipeline is validate -> checkGovernance -> commit as the human with Job: trailers -> rebase -> push, never force. Governance runs server-side because the client is not trusted.

jobs.title: Multi-project tenancy — one server hosting several repositories
jobs.description: One SpecPad server can now host several projects at once. A company with SpecPad in six repositories runs one server rather than six, with a single sign-on and per-project permissions — someone can be a committer on one project and a reader on another.
jobs.technical_notes: First slice: configuration, the repository registry, request routing, and per-project authorization. The single-repo config (repo: {...}) stays valid and is read as a one-entry registry, so existing deployments are untouched and the unprefixed /api/v1/... routes keep working when exactly one project is configured. Deferred to a second slice: the in-editor project picker and worktree reaping (Repository.release() exists but is still called by nothing, which matters more once worktrees multiply by project). Also brings the SAD current for the server as a whole, which JOB-40 did not touch.

jobs.title: Project picker and working-copy reaping — the second multi-project slice
jobs.description: On a server hosting several projects you can now switch between them from inside the editor, instead of editing the URL. The server also cleans up idle working copies, so a large deployment does not accumulate a checkout per person per project forever — never touching one that holds unpublished work.
jobs.technical_notes: Completes JOB-41. Two halves: (1) the editor gains a project switcher fed by GET /api/v1/projects, replacing the plain list of links that slice one rendered; (2) the server reaps per-user worktrees after a configurable idle period. The safety property that matters for reaping is that a working copy with uncommitted changes is never removed - a reaped draft is destroyed work with no git object behind it. Reaping must also be idempotent with an active session, since a removed copy is simply re-provisioned on next use.

jobs.title: Cut release v1.5
jobs.description: Release v1.5 — the self-hosted multi-user server, multi-project tenancy, and the fixes that landed after v1.4.
jobs.technical_notes: Release bookkeeping. Closed JOB-35..42 and set their version to v1.5; regenerated every closed job’s before/after/commits caches from git; moved the v1.4 full-document snapshot to .specpad/snapshots/v1.4 and regenerated .specpad/baseline from the v1.5 tag, freezing the verification run into it as the release’s design-verification evidence. JOB-1 stays open (perpetual foundational). JOB-35 and JOB-36 were committed with a Job: <code> trailer rather than Job: <id>, so their commit caches are recovered by matching on the code as well.

jobs.title: Software Detailed Design (SDD) pillar
jobs.description: SpecPad now tracks a Software Detailed Design alongside the requirements and tests. Each design section has a permanent identity, so requirements link to the design and the link survives any amount of rewriting, and the design itself stays free-form enough to hold diagrams and flowcharts. Requirements that point at a design section are flagged for re-review whenever that section changes.
jobs.technical_notes: The fourth register pillar, and the first that is section-and-prose rather than field-per-item. Sections carry a stable id + renameable code/title + a markdown body (images, draw.io SVGs, flowcharts), so the trace anchor is the id and headings stay free to change. Trace direction is SRS -> SDD (SrsItem.design[]), matching SrsItem.satisfies -> PRD: tests keep verifying requirements, and the matrix renders PRD -> SRS -> SDD and SRS -> VTP so the reviewer reads the path. Authoring is always at the maximum rigor (62304 Class C / FDA Enhanced); omission is an export-time decision, which keeps class/rigor out of the schema entirely and survives 62304 Ed 2 replacing A/B/C with rigor levels I/II. Section skeleton follows IEEE 1016 design viewpoints; decomposition rules in the guide follow Parnas (hide the decision likely to change; never decompose from the call flow) plus the independently-testable and safety-risk-isolation tests.

jobs.title: Document tabs by acronym, and the Auditor recognises the detailed design
jobs.description: The document tabs now read as the acronyms a regulated team already uses — PRD, SRS, SAD, SDD, VTP — with the full name on hover. The Auditor view also recognises the detailed design: Design Outputs is no longer permanently partial once both the architecture and the detailed design are present.
jobs.technical_notes: Two consistency fixes after the SDD landed. (1) Tab labels become acronyms; the full name moves to a title attribute so nothing is lost for a reader who does not know them. TAB-1 is reworded accordingly. (2) designControls gains the SDD: Design Outputs derives present/partial/gap from architecture AND detailed design rather than hard-coding the SDD as roadmap, which it stopped being in JOB-44. DC-2 reworded. Deliberately NOT in scope: making the PRD, SAD and SDD editable in every phase — that is the next job.

jobs.title: One notion of read-only: demo becomes a sandbox, and a reader sees a read-only editor
jobs.description: The demo is now a sandbox: every document can be edited, changes live only in the browser and reset on reload, and Save offers the file as a download. Separately, someone signed in to a server with a read-only role now actually sees a read-only editor, rather than being allowed to type into changes the server would refuse.
jobs.technical_notes: Both halves had the same cause: nothing answered "may I edit in this session". readOnly was passed to some views from launch.demo and to none from the server session, so the demo blocked editing on PRD/SAD/SDD/Results while leaving SRS/VTP fully editable, and a server reader could type into every table. Now one derived value - the session capability - flows to every view, and demo is no longer read-only at all. SRSTable and VTPTable gain the readOnly prop the others already had. Persisting in demo mode downloads the document instead of writing, so the sandbox has an exit. Also closes the rendering half of EDR-3, which was previously verified only at the transport level.

jobs.title: Detailed design reads as a document, and is written like one
jobs.description: The detailed design is now one continuous document you scroll, with a sticky outline that follows where you are, editing in place on the section you are reading, and drag-to-reorder. Its text has been rewritten to read like reference documentation rather than a filled-in template.
jobs.technical_notes: Two halves. (1) The view: outline-plus-single-section did not suit 55 short sections - a long index against short articles, with the editor always at the top of the pane and the management controls stranded below it. Replaced with a continuous document, scrollspy outline, per-section hover menu, and inline editing; section boundaries stay hard data because SrsItem.design points at a section id, so this is a rendering change only. (2) The prose: the guide prescribed a content checklist and the generator turned it into a form - 48 of 55 sections opened Secret: and 50 closed Acceptance:, and 69 percent sat within a third of the median length. The guide now frames the SDD as reference documentation (Diataxis: describe and only describe), names the tells to avoid, and states that length follows the unit rather than the template.

jobs.title: Author the trace links in the editor
jobs.description: The links between documents can now be edited in the browser. A requirement row expands to show and edit what it satisfies, what design implements it, and what verifies it; a design section can be linked to requirements from the design itself. References are chosen from a searchable list showing each item's code and text, so a link can no longer be mistyped.
jobs.technical_notes: Only verifies (VTP -> SRS) had an editor; satisfies (JOB-16) and design (JOB-44) were displays only, so no human could author an upward or downward trace without the skill. New RefPicker component - searchable multi-select over candidate items, value is ids, chips show codes - used for all three, which also removes the raw-id typing verifies previously required. The link stays stored on the requirement; the design view edits it by writing back to the SRS document, so there is still one home per edge. The requirement row expansion now shows the whole chain for that requirement rather than only its tests.

jobs.title: Verification links resolve to test groups, and the gate notices stale design
jobs.description: Seventy verification tests were reported as not run when their tests had in fact passed: they named a group of tests, and the matcher only accepted the full name of a single one. A test entry can now point at a group. Separately, the pre-push check now notices when a commit changes code that a design section claims to describe while that section stays untouched.
jobs.technical_notes: Two defects, both mine. (1) The run records a full test name; automation links were being written as describe-block names; matchLink required exact equality, so 70 of 243 entries resolved to nothing and the Overview read 170/243. A link selector now matches a result whose selector equals it or begins with it at a word boundary, so naming a group is legitimate and adding a test to that group does not need a spec edit. (2) The pre-push hook only ever grepped for srs|vtp, so the SAD and SDD were invisible to it - which is how JOB-40 shipped a server with no architecture update. The hook now uses each SDD section source path: a pushed commit touching a claimed path whose section body is unchanged is named as possibly stale.

jobs.title: IEC 62304 compliance gaps — findings to attack during the detailed trace
jobs.description: The register of places SpecPad did not satisfy IEC 62304, found by tracing the standard clause by clause. Sixteen gaps were recorded; JOB-56 answered most of them, and this record now says which were closed, which were answered by declaring the boundary, and which are still open under a different description.
jobs.technical_notes: GAP 1 — software units are not identifiable in the data (found 2026-08-11, JOB-44 review). An SDD item is one of three things: a group heading, a cross-cutting design view (IEEE 1016), or a software unit (62304 5.4.2). Only heading is machine-readable; unit and view are told apart by reading. Consequences: 5.4.1 asks the architecture to be refined into software UNITS and the unit list cannot be produced mechanically; 5.5.3 wants acceptance criteria per unit and cannot be rolled up; risk control measures allocate to units and will need this as a join key. Likely fix: an optional kind (unit | view) on SddSection, defaulting to unit, with the seven viewpoint sections marked view. Note also that SDD-40, SDD-47 and SDD-61 each cover several components in one section - legitimate under 5.4.1 since the manufacturer defines granularity, but it should be a declared choice rather than an artefact of how the prose was grouped. GAP 2 — SOUP performance requirements are asserted, not measured (found 2026-08-12, JOB-54 review). Five components carry a figure (react 250 rows/200ms, react-markdown 60 sections/500ms, codemirror 2000 lines/300ms, ajv 250 items/50ms, node first request/5s). All were chosen as plausible targets to satisfy the guide rule; none was benchmarked. Each is measurable with the existing suite. GAP 3 — no SOUP component links to a verifying test (tests is empty on all eleven), which is the exact audit finding the guide quotes: a requirement that reaches no test. Several are genuinely exercised — ajv by the validation and fixture suites, git by repository.integration.test.ts, the editor stack by the transport conformance suite — so the links can be made true rather than manufactured, and left empty where they are not. GAP 4 — vulnerability handling is not held anywhere (deferred 2026-08-12, JOB-55). FDA June 2025 and IEC 81001-5-1 both require a documented plan for monitoring advisories, triaging them, disclosing to users, and deploying patches to a deployed device. Deferred deliberately as post-market and operational rather than design-time; it has no home in SpecPad today, not even as prose. GAP 5 — clause 9 (software problem resolution) is absent in full (found 2026-08-12, detailed 62304 trace). No problem report, no classification by type/scope/criticality, no investigation record, no advisory to relevant parties, no trend analysis. JobType bugfix is the nearest thing and carries none of it. Highest-value of the missing processes because four other clauses discharge their obligation by referring to it: 5.6.8, 5.7.2, 6.2.2 and 8.2.4 cannot be closed while it is absent. GAP 6 — clause 5.1 (software development planning) has no artefact at all. 5.1.1 development plan, 5.1.4 standards/methods/tools (C), 5.1.5 integration test planning, 5.1.6 verification planning, 5.1.7 risk management planning, 5.1.8 documentation planning, 5.1.12 common defect identification (B/C) all have nowhere to live. Structural rather than incidental: every SpecPad register answers what is true of the product, none answers how the project will be run, so the SDP is written elsewhere and drifts from the registers meant to implement it. GAP 7 — clause 6 (maintenance) is mostly absent: 6.1 maintenance plan, 6.2.1 feedback intake, 6.2.5 communication to users and regulators. 6.2.3/6.2.4 are partial — jobs are change requests with an owner and status but carry no impact analysis and no approval record. Note 6.2.5 is GAP 4 seen from the safety side rather than the security side; one mechanism would answer both. GAP 8 — 5.8.2/5.8.3 (known residual anomalies at release) have no home, and this was conflated with the SOUP decision. Removing anomalies from the SOUP register was about a supplier published defect list against a moving feed (7.1.3) and that reasoning holds. It says nothing about the product own known defects at release, which 5.8.2 requires. Every release ships with known bugs and there is nowhere to record them or their risk evaluation. GAP 9 — the VTP has no test level, so 5.5 unit verification, 5.6 integration testing and 5.7 system testing cannot be told apart. 62304 treats them as three activities with distinct records; SpecPad has one flat register, so a manufacturer can show requirements are covered by something but not that each activity was performed. Small schema change (a level field), large return. Related: 5.6.7/5.7.5 record contents are partial — the run is captured but tester identity and test environment are not. GAP 10 — 5.2.2 requirement content categories are not prompted or checkable. The nine categories (functional, inputs/outputs, interfaces, alarms, security, usability, data definition, installation and acceptance, maintenance, regulatory) appear nowhere in the schema or in guides/requirements.md. A reviewer asking to see the security requirements can only be answered by reading all of them. The categories work like STRIDE does for threats: the value is the coverage prompt, not the label. GAP 11 — 5.5.3/5.5.4 unit acceptance criteria are prose only. guides/detailed-design.md asks for them where not self-evident, so careful authors write them, but they sit inside markdown and cannot be rolled up per unit, governed, or shown as a list. 5.5.4 Class C criteria (event sequencing, resource use, fault handling, boundary values) have no structure at all. Same shape as GAP 3: the guide asks, nothing can find it. GAP 12 — 7.1.5 and 7.3.2 (sequences of events) are not modelled. RiskItem.text holds the hazardous situation; there is no field for the sequence of events that leads to it, nor for a new sequence introduced by a control. ISO 14971 and 62304 both treat the sequence as the analysis rather than decoration. GAP 13 — 5.3.5 segregation for risk control (Class C) is not recorded, nor the rationale that the segregation is effective, which A1:2015 strengthened. Nothing in the SAD or SDD marks two items as segregated or says why the separation holds. GAP 14 — 4.3 safety classification is absent by decision, and the decision confuses two things. Authoring at maximum rigor always is defensible and is written down in SKILL.md; 4.3 nonetheless asks for the classification and its rationale as a record, so a submission that never states a class has over-delivered on content while omitting the declaration. The fix is not class-based filtering but letting a project declare its class and why, while still authoring at full rigor. Lands on Ed 2 two-level scheme when it publishes (~May 2027). GAP 15 — 4.4 legacy software has no route. A1:2015 gives an explicit path for software predating the standard: gap analysis plus a risk-based justification of the closure plan. The baseline generator is the mechanism for drafting a spec from existing code, but nothing records the 4.4 justification that makes it acceptable. GAP 16 — 5.8.5 (how the software was created) and 5.8.8 (repeatability of the release) are absent. releases.json records version, ref, date, author and snapshot, but not the toolchain, build environment or anything that would let the release be reproduced. 5.8.7 archival is partial: git tags exist, no retention period is stated. DEFECT found by the trace (fixed 2026-08-12) — SKILL.md documented a soup-anomalies governance rule for a release after the rule was removed, and skill/__tests__/parity.test.ts stayed green because its second assertion matched a fixed list of five legacy rule names and never looked at the prd-, sdd-, risk-, soup- or threat- namespaces. Parity now matches by namespace, with an explicit allowlist for active-job-required-for-spec-changes, which is a skill-side pre-commit gate needing HEAD rather than a data-only rule. CLOSING LEDGER (2026-08-13). Closed outright: GAP 1 (units identifiable — done by JOB-52's `kind`, and never marked; corrected here), GAP 9 (verification level, field plus 277 tests backfilled), GAP 10 (5.2.2 categories, field plus 273 requirements backfilled — and the enum corrected from ten values to the full a)–l) twelve). Answered by declaring the boundary rather than building anything: GAP 4 (vulnerability handling), GAP 5 (clause 9), GAP 6 (5.1 planning), GAP 7 (clause 6 maintenance), GAP 15 (4.4 legacy). These are now named in the Planning view as processes held elsewhere, with the kind of system that holds each. A references register was built to point at specific documents and then removed: a quality system already indexes its own documents and a second index in a repository is the one that goes stale. STILL OPEN, under a new description: GAP 8, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 16 each gained a field and no data. Measured at close — safetyClass not declared; 0 of 49 units state acceptance criteria; 0 of 12 risks record a sequence of events; 0 of 9 releases record known anomalies or a build; no segregation claimed (correctly, none exists). GAP 2 and GAP 3 are untouched: SOUP performance figures are still asserted rather than measured, and 0 of 11 components link to a verifying test. The shape of what remains is one thing rather than eight: SpecPad can now hold what 62304 asks for, and largely does not hold it about itself. That is a content job, not a contract job, and it is the natural acceptance test for JOB-57 — a skill that drafts these fields properly would fill them.

jobs.title: Software risk pillar (IEC 62304 clause 7)
jobs.description: SpecPad now records software risk: the hazardous situations software can contribute to, which parts of the design could cause them, and the requirements that control them. Because a control is an ordinary requirement, the tests already verifying it become the evidence that the control works.
jobs.technical_notes: The 62304 clause 7 slice only. Hazards, harms, P1/P2 estimation, benefit-risk and post-market stay in the system risk management file the QMS owns and are referenced by id - SpecPad produces design-control evidence, not a QMS. Probability is deliberately absent: for software you cannot argue it down, so severity drives the analysis. Chain is hazardous situation -> contributing software item (SDD section) -> risk control measure (SRS requirement, per 5.2.2) -> verification, and the last link already exists via the SRS/VTP trace and captured runs, so 7.3 is largely satisfied by machinery already built. Controls are stored on the risk item. Also closes JOB-51 gap 1: SddSection gains kind (unit | view) so a cause points at a real software unit and the unit list 5.4.1 asks for becomes derivable. Security risk is deliberately NOT in this register - 62304 Ed 2 and AAMI SW96 make it a separate process, and the threat-model pillar will get its own.

jobs.description: Release v1.7 — the software risk pillar, and the editor view that makes a control verifiable at a glance.

Closed JOB-52 and set version v1.7 on it; regenerated every closed job cache; moved the v1.6 snapshot to .specpad/snapshots/v1.6 and regenerated .specpad/baseline as the v1.7 document set - now including the risk register - with the verification run frozen in. Tag on da5c398, the last content commit. jobs.title: SOUP / OTS pillar (IEC 62304 and the FDA off-the-shelf software guidance)
jobs.description: SpecPad now records the third-party software a product depends on: what it is and exactly which version, what the product requires of it, what it needs to run, what is known to be wrong with it, and what happens when the vendor stops supporting it. A component can be named as the cause of a risk, like any other part of the design.
jobs.technical_notes: Covers both regimes rather than either alone. IEC 62304 8.1.2 (identity), 5.3.3 (functional and performance requirements placed on the component), 5.3.4 (hardware and software it needs), 7.1.2/7.1.3 (published anomaly list, evaluated per version); FDA off-the-shelf guidance of August 2023 (release date, purpose and functional role, expected design limitations, current defect list, testing, and the Enhanced-level maintenance, support and end-of-life contingency). Authored at maximum rigour; Basic vs Enhanced is an export decision. Requirements placed on a component are text on the record, not SRS entries - they are requirements on a vendor, and the SRS holds only what SpecPad itself implements. RiskItem.causes extended to accept a SOUP id as well as a design unit: a cause is whatever could fail. SBOM is deliberately out of scope and separate - it is a recursive inventory of every dependency generated from the manifests, while this is the far smaller set actually assessed; conflating them would let a 40-entry assessed list pass as a 900-package inventory.

jobs.title: Cybersecurity: threat model and security architecture
jobs.description: SpecPad now records the threats against a product and what defends it, alongside a security architecture document covering the four views a submission is expected to contain. A threat is assessed on how exploitable it is rather than how probable, and where exploiting it could harm someone it links to the safety risk it creates. The architecture views carry diagrams rather than prose alone: one system-level overview and a view per deployment, the multi-patient harm path with the gates that interrupt it, the end-to-end update path, and a call flow for signing in and publishing. Every connection is labelled with what it carries, and each view lists the paths between its parts with what protects them.
jobs.technical_notes: FDA 3 February 2026 ("Quality Management System Considerations") is the edition in force, superseding June 2025 and aligning the guidance with the QMSR. Its substance carried forward from September 2023: 524B obligations, SPDF embedded in design controls, threat modelling an explicit expectation, SBOM required. IEC 81001-5-1 runs alongside as the security development lifecycle, with AAMI SW96/TIR57 for security risk management. One register rather than two: assessing a threat and identifying it are the same act, which is how SW96 treats it. Exploitability replaces probability - the structural echo of the safety risk register dropping probability, for the opposite reason: software fails deterministically, an attacker chooses when. A threat links to the safety risk it creates, which is the join SW96 exists to make. Security architecture is a separate prose document rather than SAD sections, chosen for a submission-shaped artefact; the risk is two descriptions of one system drifting, mitigated by the SAD referencing it.  SBOM remains separate. Second slice (architecture views): the guidance names four view TYPES and then says explicitly that a singular global view need not carry every data flow - additional views may detail the communications - so the count is a floor, not a target. Views are drawn to the Positron draw.io style guide v2.2. There is no SVG rasteriser in this environment, so the generator checks geometry arithmetically instead of by eye (label/shape collision, canvas overflow, crossing budget); that caught an overlapping label and two call-flow labels running off the canvas. Appendix 2.B asks for roughly nineteen details per communication path, too many for a diagram, so they sit in a per-view table plus prose on unused interfaces, handoffs, cryptography, sessions and error behaviour. Traceability is pointed at rather than restated: element -> threat causes/controls -> requirement -> test already exists and a copy would drift. Bug found on the way: loadDiagrams scanned only the arc42 text, so a figure referenced solely by the security document never loaded - every new figure would have rendered as a named gap. Figures are generated SVG, not draw.io round-trippable; if they need editing in draw.io later the generator must embed mxGraph source in the SVG content attribute. Vulnerability handling remains deferred as JOB-51 gap 4.

jobs.title: Draft to the standard: close the IEC 62304 gaps in what the skill produces
jobs.description: SpecPad now asks for the things IEC 62304 expects and records where the processes it does not own are kept. A project declares its safety class, points at the SOPs and trackers that hold its planning, maintenance and problem resolution, and is prompted for the detail a reviewer looks for rather than being left to remember it. The Auditor view became Planning: what the project follows, how it works, and where the processes it does not hold are kept. Security controls are grouped by the categories FDA expects them to be drawn from, and traceability now shows the whole chain rather than requirements and tests alone.
jobs.technical_notes: Closes the gaps found by the clause-by-clause trace (JOB-51 gaps 5-16). Decisions taken before building: (1) guides plus new fields on existing registers, no new pillars, with one exception - a minimal references register for external controlled documents; (2) the process clauses SpecPad does not own (5.1 planning, 6 maintenance, 9 problem resolution) are DECLARED and LINKED rather than modelled, following the hazardRef precedent, because most companies hold them in a QMS or tracker and duplicating that puts SpecPad in the tracker business it has avoided; (3) governance gains a non-blocking ADVISORY tier - required because the classification decision needs a way to say "out of scope for this class" without failing, and because a blocking category rule would fire on 273 existing requirements and 277 tests on day one; a project promotes an advisory to blocking by naming the rule in the index; (4) safety class is declared with a rationale and authoring stays at maximum rigor, with material beyond the declared class highlighted rather than omitted; (5) backfilling SpecPad's own 273 requirements is deliberately a later job - scripting best-guess values is exactly what produced gaps 2 and 3 in the SOUP register. Delivered across five slices. (1) Foundations: the advisory tier, safety class, and a references register. (2) Fields for what was living in prose — acceptance criteria, segregation, sequence of events, release anomalies and build record. (3) The guides, which is where a draft's quality is actually decided. (4) The editor. (5) The backfill: 273 requirements categorised and 277 tests levelled by reading each one. Two reversals, both right. `category` became an array once A1:2015 NOTE 10 was read — "the requirements in a) through l) can overlap" — and reading the amendment for that also showed the enum was missing IT-network aspects entirely, had conflated i) with k), and used the pre-amendment wording for f). The references register was built and then removed: it duplicated an index the quality system already keeps. Its purpose survives in Planning as prose. The threat model went from 9 threats to 24 by walking STRIDE across each element of the design rather than listing attacks — which is what found argument injection into git, a symlink in the seam between two controls, a direct push that never meets the commit gate, and that nothing is logged anywhere. 11 of 24 carry a justification instead of a control; that number is the output, not a defect. Found along the way: src/index.css was never imported, so the advisory styling shipped as dead code until it was noticed; and the arch diff never included sec.md, so its figures read as added files while the prose referencing them was never diffed. Not done, deliberately: SpecPad's own data does not fill the fields this job added — see JOB-51's closing ledger.

jobs.title: Make the skill self-sufficient: a fresh repository should reach the same place
jobs.description: The skill now works in passes rather than one sweep, so adopting SpecPad on an existing codebase produces a specification with real depth rather than a list of what each module does. Tests are expected to attack a requirement as well as demonstrate it, and the security testing FDA asks for is recorded in a form a reviewer can be pointed at.
jobs.technical_notes: Opened because the dogfooding has been testing the skill's CONTENT, not its INVOCATION. Across this session the skill was never invoked once: the working loop was followed from the summary in CLAUDE.md, and SKILL.md was read as a document being edited rather than experienced as a user's Claude experiences it — cold, triggered by a phrase, with no prior context. Those are different tests and only the second one says whether the skill works for someone who is not already holding the design in their head. The measurable damage: SKILL.md says to read the matching guide before writing each kind of entry. 33 requirements and 33 tests were written this session and guides/requirements.md was read once — while being edited, never before authoring. 17 of the 33 requirements carry more than one rule against a guide that says to split them; TR-12 enumerates four separate reports, GOV-22 covers two subjects and needed two governance rules to serve it, SEC-8 runs to 57 words. The pre-existing corpus is no better (155 of 264), so this is a standing weakness the guide describes and nothing enforces. Scope: (a) split the requirements that carry several rules, starting with TR-12, GOV-22 and SEC-8; (b) make the skill self-sufficient so it does not lean on CLAUDE.md, which a fresh repository will not have; (c) make guide-reading structural rather than an instruction that can be skipped; (d) an acceptance test — run the skill cold against a repository it has never seen and judge the result against what this repository holds. The second acceptance test worth running is the same skill against THIS repository: JOB-51's ledger shows six fields that exist and hold nothing about SpecPad itself, and a skill that drafts them properly would fill them. ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE (2026-08-14). The generator was run cold against src/shared/ twice — once single-sweep, once with the multi-pass procedure — and both compared against the curated register for the same subsystem. Requirements 35 -> 88 against a curated 93; tests 35 -> 126 against 95; tests per requirement 1.00 -> 1.43 against a curated 1.02; non-nominal tests 0 -> 36 against 2; security tests 0 -> 5 against 0. Which pass earned what: pass 2 enumerating rather than abstracting took governance from 1 requirement to 22, because reading the rule list is not the same as summarising the file. Pass 3 (what the code refuses) found the refusals no API surface shows — reject a non-object distinctly from a schema error, name the unrecognised type, raise after the retry bound rather than return a duplicate. Pass 4 (tests as intent) was richest: merge went from 4 requirements to 16, every one a decision recorded only in a test name — same value on both sides is not a conflict, conflicts are per field not per item, the local value stays so the document remains valid, an added item lands beside the neighbour it followed. Pass 5 caught the invariants that live in no single file. Two results worth keeping. The multi-pass output now EXCEEDS the curated register on verification depth (126 tests vs 95, 36 non-nominal vs 2) — the generator produces a better protocol than the repository it was generated from, which makes the backfill case concrete rather than theoretical. And governance caught a real error mid-run: the first attempt had four dangling verifies because headings shared the id counter, and referential-integrity named all four. What no pass recovered, structurally: the why, the rejected alternative, the corner case found by a bug, and intent — the PRD is 7 proposed items against a curated 34. A baseline is the scaffold that makes the working loop possible, not a substitute for having run it. 54 vtp-negative-path advisories remain on the cold output: the generator gave depth where code and tests justified it and left the rest nominal rather than inventing boundary cases, which is the correct behaviour and an honest record of what is left. CLOSING LEDGER. Delivered: the multi-pass baseline (survey, behaviour, what the code refuses, tests as intent, invariants, then VTP, security testing, PRD and a starter SAD); the four defects the first cold run exposed (draft is a field again, the SAD step is no longer skippable, the baseline asks for the safety class, securityControl is named); the VTP depth model (kind, securityTest, vtp-negative-path) with FDA V.C taxonomy; three fixes for gaps this session demonstrated (sdd-unit-trace, skill-to-schema field parity, and the CLAUDE directive pointing at the skill instead of restating it); the design pass, which also found all 24 requirements added this session mis-traced to design views; and the scope item that nearly got skipped — TR-12, GOV-22 and SEC-8 split into eight requirements with four more tests. NOT DONE, deliberately: the register is still 52% multi-clause (161 of 308). Splitting three requirements does not move a corpus-wide number, and an advisory rule for it was considered and rejected — 161 findings would teach people to ignore the advisory tier, which is the thing the tier was built to protect. It belongs to the requirement audit, which proposes rather than enforces. Two hygiene items also left: the release-cut fields are still prose rather than a numbered step (0 of 9 releases record anomalies or a build), and nothing surfaces the draft ratio, so a project that is mostly unratified scaffold still looks like one that is specified.

jobs.title: Marketing site: lead with medical-device compliance, and give the big features their own pages
jobs.description: The site now says what SpecPad became. It leads with IEC 62304 and FDA compliance rather than general requirements management, lists the capabilities on the front page, and gives the features with real depth — traceability and standards, the self-hosted server, cybersecurity, risk and third-party software, and deployment — a page each.
jobs.technical_notes: The positioning had drifted from the product: the site described a general requirements tool that suited regulated work, while the product had grown seven pillars, clause-by-clause conformity against four standards, and a security architecture. Medical-device first throughout, with general use still true and still mentioned, because the core skill genuinely is domain-neutral and the medical layer is an add-on. Derived content is generated from src/shared at build time, following generate-reference.ts: rule tables, document types, control categories and clause tables cannot drift from the product, and prose stays hand-written. This is the same reasoning that removed the references register and the CLAUDE.md loop summary — a second copy is the one that goes stale.

jobs.title: Review passes: a fresh look at what was just written
jobs.description: Documents the skill produces are now reviewed by a separate pass that has not seen the reasoning behind them — one that checks the citations against their sources, one that argues the approach was wrong, and one that asks what the code handles that the document does not mention.
jobs.technical_notes: Opened from the observation that self-review is the weakest check available. Across this session the things actually caught were caught mechanically — referential-integrity found four dangling verifies, tsc found the level name collision, the parity test found a rule documented after removal, the link test found a missing template. Re-reading my own work caught comparatively little, and the citation errors (FDA June 2025 for February 2026, nine categories for twelve, the pre-amendment wording for f) were found only by opening the source document. A review in the same context as the generation agrees with itself. The fix is a sub-process with a fresh context that receives the artefact and the sources but NOT the reasoning that produced it.

jobs.title: Citations, and an auditor that can check them
jobs.description: Requirements record the construct they rest on, so a later reader can open it rather than take the requirement's word for it. A separate audit pass then checks the register against those sources and against itself, and a release cannot be cut while its findings are unreviewed.
jobs.technical_notes: Opened after three mechanical staleness checks were prototyped and all three failed: requirement-unchanged-while-source-changed caught 9 of 18 known-stale requirements while flagging 176; source-newer-than-prose flagged 278 of 316; absent-identifier found one false positive. They fail for one reason — the finest trace the register holds is a file, and the hot files change every job. Citations give the audit something exact to open, which is what makes the check affordable and what makes a finding checkable.

jobs.title: One skill, aimed at medical devices
jobs.description: SpecPad is a medical-device offering rather than a general tool with a regulated add-on. The optional specpad-medical skill folds into core, there is one architecture profile, and init no longer asks which kind of project this is.
jobs.technical_notes: The split had already stopped paying for itself: core carried safety classification, IEC 62304 risk, SOUP, cybersecurity, the design-control map and the standards conformance view, while the add-on was 56 lines of SKILL.md and two templates — one of which is the generic template plus a segregation section and an architecture-verification section. The audit surfaced it as four separate contradictions (CORE-2, CORE-3, SAD-5, SAD-6) because the register still described the split as the design.

jobs.title: Cut release v2.0
jobs.description: SpecPad 2.0: a medical-device design-controls tool rather than a general spec editor. Nine jobs — the cybersecurity architecture and threat model, SOUP, the advisory governance tier, citations and a runnable audit, the review passes, the marketing site, and the collapse of the medical add-on into one skill.
jobs.technical_notes: Scope: JOB-51, 54, 55, 56, 57, 58, 59, 60, 61. Tag points at the last feature commit (the audit script); the cut bookkeeping follows it, as in v1.4 through v1.7.
